message: The data field describes every command. Run oe help <command> for one command.

commands.name: new
commands.summary: Create a project and its Sandbox environment, then write open-e2ee.config.ts, the Relay connection in .env.local, and the @open-e2ee/oe devDependency.

commands.name: auth
commands.summary: Log in with a browser and store the session in the OS keychain, then accept the OpenE2EE terms for the organization. --organization ORG puts the session in that organization. Without it, a person at a terminal who belongs to more than one organization chooses one. In an app directory with no config, a person at a terminal then creates a project, links one, or skips. Show the session and its organizations, or remove the session.

commands.name: org
commands.summary: Show the organization of the current session, list the organizations of the account, or move the stored session to another organization. ORG is an ID or a unique name. Without ORG, a person at a terminal chooses one. A session from OE_ACCESS_TOKEN or an agent session cannot switch.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check the config, session, project, and Relay connection of the selected environment. With --wait, then wait for the first acknowledged Sandbox message.

commands.name: identity
commands.summary:
Check a public draft identity profile. External ES256 checks send a fresh registration assertion from stdin to the authenticated Console verifier. The assertion is transient. Device-owned checks use no assertion. Results are historical and do not verify installed configuration, device admission, member binding, exchange or lifecycle. Current and dry-run read installed authority. Selection, keys rotation and lifecycle use exact retained operations. Production changes need explicit consent. First-use declarations need literal --env.

For normal key rotation, add the new public key while keeping the old key. Start signing with the new key. Remove the old key after its assertions expire, including clock tolerance. Key removal does not revoke existing device credentials. Registered devices can still renew with a device proof.

Suspension refuses registration, linking, renewal, recovery and identified requests. It keeps account data and devices. Stop issuing assertions for suspended members in your application. Use oe identity lifecycle activate for a new change, subject to current authority guards. Use oe identity operation resume to continue the retained lifecycle change. Permanently revoked devices stay revoked.

Previously issued anonymous capabilities, attachment URLs, sender certificates and group tokens keep their independent expiry and policy. Relay cannot recall downloaded or decrypted content. Provider sign-in cannot recover a lost device-owned account key. See https://docs.open-e2ee.dev/relay for the key rotation and account lifecycle procedures.
usage: oe identity keys rotate --keys PATH [--dry-run] [--yes] [--confirm-state-never-used] [--confirm-slot-never-used] [--env sandbox|production]
oe identity operation status --kind selection|keys-only|lifecycle [--env sandbox|production]
oe identity operation retry --kind selection|keys-only [--yes] [--env sandbox|production]
oe identity operation resume --kind lifecycle [--yes] [--env sandbox|production]
oe identity operation cancel --kind selection|keys-only [--yes] [--env sandbox|production]

commands.name: link
commands.summary: Link this directory to a Relay project that exists and write the Relay connection of each active environment to its env file. With no config, write open-e2ee.config.ts from the server policy. Without PROJECT, rewrite only the env files.

commands.name: project
commands.summary: Show the linked Relay project, list the projects of the organization of the session, show usage, or print a Relay connection URL.

commands.name: config
commands.summary: Keep open-e2ee.config.ts and the console in step. push applies the environment sections: Sandbox, then Production when the file has its section. pull writes the Relay policy of each active environment into the file with the fewest changes. A Production change or a replaced value needs --yes or a person's answer. --dry-run changes nothing. Optional identity fields apply only to their environment. Pull --identity adds those fields explicitly. Identity push needs literal --env. Inactive Production activates before a later identity preview.

commands.name: notifications
commands.summary: Stage and verify best-effort iOS notification profiles.
usage: oe notifications setup ios [--profile background-only|visible-alert] [--env sandbox|production]
oe notifications verify ios [--app-bundle PATH] [--env sandbox|production]

commands.name: agent
commands.summary: Install the OpenE2EE skills for coding agents: write .agents/skills/<name> and link .claude/skills/<name> to it, or write a copy when a link fails. The project scope uses the directory of open-e2ee.config.ts, else the working directory, and --scope user uses the home directory. --check reports each skill as current, missing, or changed, and writes nothing.

commands.name: help
commands.summary: Show all commands, or the usage of one command.

environmentVariables.name: OE_ACCESS_TOKEN
environmentVariables.summary: A scoped CI credential. It takes precedence over the stored session, and oe auth login never replaces it. The CLI keeps it in memory and never stores it.

environmentVariables.name: OE_ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPES
environmentVariables.summary: The scopes of OE_ACCESS_TOKEN, separated by commas or spaces.

environmentVariables.name: OE_PROTECTION_BYPASS
environmentVariables.summary: A protection bypass secret for the control URL. Login stores it with that session. It takes precedence over the stored bypass and never appears in output.

environmentVariables.name: OE_ENV
environmentVariables.summary: The environment of doctor, identity, project, and notifications when --env is not given: sandbox or production. new and config ignore it.

environmentVariables.name: OE_OPERATION_ID
environmentVariables.summary: The idempotency key for each nonidentity remote mutation of one run. For identity, it confirms only an exact retained original or cancellation. It cannot create or replace an operation.

exitCodes.meaning: The command failed. The error and its code tell why.
The command line is invalid or a required input is missing.

Authentication is required. Run next, which is oe auth login, with --organization ORG after a failed switch. ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID has no next: set OE_ACCESS_TOKEN to a new token, or unset it and run oe auth login.
A person must act before the command can continue. The error tells what to do. When action.url is present, it is the page that the person opens.
The failure is temporary. Run next later. Identity next preserves the exact retained operation and never creates a replacement.

globalFlags.name: --json
globalFlags.summary: Write one JSON document to stdout for the result, for success and for failure. oe auth login writes one pending event before it, while a person approves the device.

globalFlags.name: --json-stream
globalFlags.summary: Write newline-delimited JSON progress events, then one final event, to stdout.

globalFlags.name: --agent yes|no|auto
globalFlags.summary: Say whether a coding agent runs oe. The default, auto, reads the environment variables that coding agents set. Under an agent, the default output is JSON, and oe never prompts and never opens a browser. --agent no restores text output.

globalFlags.name: --env sandbox|production
globalFlags.summary: Select the environment. -e is the short form. Without it, doctor, identity, project, and notifications read OE_ENV, then use sandbox. config pull reads each active environment, and config push applies each section of the config; --env narrows either to one.

globalFlags.name: --control-url URL
globalFlags.summary: Use another control API. It must use HTTPS except on loopback.
